name: Ace of Clubs
description:
The Ace of Clubs brings together a variety of students who enjoy playing games, including board games, card games, word games, strategy games, online games, and more! We are a fun and welcoming environment, and we also have snacks!!

We meet every Thursday night from 7-9 PM in Plyler 026.
summary: Board Game club is an opportunity to escape the stresses of school, meet new people, learn new games, and have fun! We play a variety of games each week, from board games to card games to games online! Feel free to bring your games and your friends!

name: Acts of Random Kindness Club
description:
The mission of the Acts of Random Kindness Club, or A.R.K Club, is to uplift all students and staff within Furman University, as well as members of our community, through random and intentional acts of kindness. We wish to promote positivity, unity, and compassion in both learning and non-academic environments. We also wish to enhance Furman University‘s social and academic value by encouraging students to live as positive people and motivators, using kindness to change this world!
 
Some of our goals include:
- Placing an emphasis on inclusion and unity
- Making a difference in the lives of students and faculty
- Spreading joy and fun on our campus in creative ways
- Focusing on mental health
- Advocating for students through acts of kindness and support
 
Join our ARK Club GroupMe for the 2025-26 school year here!
 
Follow us on the ARK Club Instagram page here!
 
Read our story on Furman News here!
summary: The mission of the Acts of Random Kindness Club is to uplift all students and staff within Furman University, as well as members of our community, through random and intentional acts of kindness! Join us as we promote positivity, compassion, and unity!

name: Adelphian and Philosophian Debate Society
description: The Adelphian and Philosophian Debate Society is a student-led organization dedicated to creating an open space for debate and conversation on campus. In the past we have attended debate competitions and hosted debate competitions for High Schools. Our faculty advisor is Dr. Brandon Inabinet in the Communications department.
summary: The Adelphian and Philosophian Debate Society is a student-led organization dedicated to creating an open space for debate and conversation on campus.

name: Admission Ambassadors
description:
Hi Class of 2025! Admissions Ambassadors is a student group operated out of the Office of Admissions to recruit prospective high school students to Furman. Activities include giving walking/riding tours, hosting lunches, sitting on student panels, assisting with virtual recruiting events, and on-campus major visit events. 

 

The Office of Admissions will solicit for new applications at the start of the Fall 2021 school semester for current sophomores, juniors, and seniors. Another application and selection round will take place in Spring 2022!
summary: Student organization to recruit prospective high school students to Furman.  Activities include giving walking/riding tours, hosting lunches, sitting on student panels, and major visit events.

name: Afrikiya
description:
This organization has the purpose to enlighten Furman campus about African history, countries, cities and the realities of being an African or being from the diaspora. This organization will not tolerate racist comments, discrimination, homophobia, xenophobia and portrayal of stereotypes.

For the 2024-2025 Academic Year, we will meet biweekly every Thursday from 5:30 pm - 6:15 pm in HIPP HALL 106. For meeting updates and other important information, join our  Groupme chat. Or follow our Instagram: afrikiya_fu.

description: Here you will find a great group of remarkable, intelligent, and committed young women who are dedicated to their sisters and to Alpha Delta Pi. name: Alpha Epsilon Delta
description:
The objectives of Alpha Epsilon Delta are to encourage excellence in pre-health scholarship, to stimulate an appreciation of the importance of pre-health education, and to promote cooperation and contacts between healthcare professionals and pre-health students.

We will host a plethora of events & meetings throughout the semester to advance pre-health goals. Some of our events include Mock Interviews, Mentoring Events, MMI Practice, and a Mock MCAT. Additionally, we host a variety of CLPs, Blood Drives, and other community outreach programs.

name: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated (Rho Zeta Chapter)
description: Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Inc., Rho Zeta Chapter was established at Furman University on May 1, 1994 and holds the title as the first, and only, historically African-American sorority chartered on the campus. While historically African American, we welcome members from all ethnic and religious backgrounds.

name: Alpha Phi Omega
description:
Alpha Phi Omega is a co-ed Service Fraternity open to anyone of any race, gender, sexuality, or affiliation to any other groups on campus (including Greek organizations). Founded in 1925, Alpha Phi Omega is the largest collegiate fraternity in the United States, with chapters at over 350 campuses, an active membership of over 25,000 students, and over 500,000 alumni members. This is the Alpha Eta Nu Chapter, which was first chartered on May 3rd, 2014. Focusing on helping others, our organization is founded on service which facilitates the strong fellowship found between our brothers, best exemplified in our motto, "Be a leader, be a friend, be of service."

Meetings on Wednesdays at 7 pm in Furman 214

name: Beta Beta Beta Biological Honor Society
description:
TriBeta is an organization for students interested in the biological sciences. TriBeta meets once a month, participates in outside activities, provides service opportunities, and helps bring speakers to campus. Service opportunities include educating students from elementary to high school in the biological sciences and fundraising for the American Cancer Society. 

Full members of the Honor Society receive cords to wear at graduation. Requirements to be a Full member: - at least a 3.0 in biology courses - taken at least 3 courses in biology (this does include AP) - majoring in biology (some exceptions, such as for neuroscience). If any of these do not apply then you are eligible for an Associate membership only and can be upgraded when requirements are fulfilled.
summary: TriBeta is an organization for students interested in the biological sciences. TriBeta meets once a month, participates in outside activities, provides service opportunities, and helps bring speakers to campus.

The Gamma Xi chapter at Furman University was founded in 1994. name: Delta Gamma

The Founders sought to maintain high ideals of friendship among women, promote educational and cultural interests, and to create a true sense of social responsibility and service in order to exemplify college women at their best. Delta Gammas membership has grown to more than 250,000 women worldwide with 150 collegiate chapters and more than 200 alumnae groups across the United States and Canada.

name: Furman Bands
description: The Furman Bands are among the oldest college bands in the South, having been initiated in 1920. The band program consists of five major ensembles: the Symphonic Band, the Wind Ensemble, the Basketball Band, the Paladin Regiment and the Jazz Ensemble. Over 60 percent of the band members major in disciplines other than music. Supplementing these groups are various smaller ensembles in percussion, woodwind and brass. Auditions for the Symphonic Band are held at the beginning of every semester, while auditions for the jazz ensemble are held are held each fall. A grade point average of 2.0 is required for most ensembles. Students from across campus can make music as members of the Furman Bands no matter their chosen area of academic study. We have room for YOU!

name: Furman University Aikido Club
description:
Aikido is a modern Japanese martial art that specializes in self defense and mind-body wellness. It focuses on the redirection of motion by using joint techniques and throws, while maintaining mental focus. 

Our club meets Mondays and Wednesdays from 3:30-5:00 to train in the Dance Studio on the second floor of the Furman Physical Activities Center. Beginners are welcome!

The Furman University Aikido Club strives to promote personal well-being and harmony in daily life for all its members through martial arts training, specifically Ki Development and Shinshin Toitsu Aikido as taught by Master Koichi Tohei Sensei. Ki-Aikido emphasizes realizing the natural and original state of unity between mind and body and between self and the universe. Realizing this unity leads students to achieve their full potential in the classroom, at work, in athletics, the performing arts, and in daily life. The Furman University Aikido Club seeks to provide the means by which students can benefit from learning the principles of mind and body coordination. These principles can be learned by men and women of all ages. From children to senior citizens, we encourage everyone to practice together in a safe, compassionate manner. While Aikido is a Japanese art and we wish to preserve its beautiful traditions, anyone, regardless of philosophical and religious persuasion, is always a very welcome member of our organization.

name: Furman University Libraries
description:
Why are our libraries among the top ranked in the nation for student satisfaction? We seek to engage, enlighten, and empower our students and provide them with the resources and services to excel in their studies. Whether you're researching the work of a 19th century artist or seeking the latest finding in a cell biology journal, Furman's library system can help. Our friendly and knowledgeable librarians are devoted to student learning and research support. They can help navigate our collection of more than one million resources, including books, e-books, journals, films, music, images and electronic databases. 
 
 The centerpiece of the library system is the James B. Duke Library, which houses more than 600,000 volumes. Take advantage of our Special Collections to find unique historical documents, photographs and artifacts or browse for digital versions of some of these resources through the Digital Collections Center. If you’re looking for specialized libraries located closer to your classes, visit the Sanders Science Library or the Maxwell Music Library.  With so many options available, it’s no surprise that our libraries are a frequent destination for studying, meeting friends, conducting research, and enjoying campus events. 

 

JAMES B. DUKE LIBRARY
 With everything from a 24-hour study room to a wealth of academic resources, our main library is the intellectual center of the university. Study with us.

SPECIAL COLLECTIONS AND ARCHIVES
 Browse photographs, manuscripts, artifacts, and books that document the history of Furman, South Carolina Baptists, notable local poets, and the Upstate. 

DIGITAL COLLECTIONS CENTER
 Explore over 50,000 unique digital resources online. We provide access to photographs, books, oral histories, videos, manuscripts, and more. Go digital.

MAXWELL MUSIC LIBRARY
 The Robert J. Maxwell Music Media Center and Library offers a wealth of resources that other schools our size simply don't have. Listen in our music library.

SANDERS SCIENCE LIBRARY
 Looking for resources, expert help, or a great place to study? The science library will help you bridge your education between the classroom and lab. Conduct research.
summary: Furman University is a school driven by academics and has amazing resources to support our students, including three libraries, digital collection, and special collections

This not only benefits our members but also enriches the overall cultural awareness of the Furman community. By learning about the customs, languages, art, and cuisines of this region, our organization will help bridge cultural gaps and promote a more inclusive campus environment. Fostering Inclusivity: Our organization is committed to creating an inclusive space for all students, regardless of their backgrounds. By celebrating the diversity within the MENA region, we provide an opportunity for students to engage with and appreciate different perspectives, ultimately fostering a more inclusive campus community. Community Engagement: FU MENA will actively engage with the larger community through cultural events, volunteering, and collaborative initiatives. By connecting with local organizations and businesses, we hope to strengthen Furman's ties with the broader community while also showcasing the importance of intercultural dialogue and cooperation. Religious and Spiritual Understanding: While FU MENA is not primarily a religious organization, the MENA region is home to various religious traditions, including Islam, Christianity, Judaism, and others. We aim to provide a platform for open and respectful discussions about religion and spirituality in the context of the MENA region, contributing to a vibrant religious and spiritual community at Furman.

F.U. MENA is to spread awareness about the MENA region. We will showcase the food, dance, and music of the MENA region.

name: Furman University Office of Spiritual Life
description:
For many, college may be the first time you're exploring faith away from home. We're here to act as a sounding board for whatever questions you might have. Maybe you've grown up in one faith but have always been curious about another, or maybe you didn't grow up in a particular faith tradition and want to know how to start the conversation. Maybe you want to talk with someone about how what you've learned from your church, temple, mosque, or synagogue connect with what you're learning in class. Whatever your faith questions might be, we're glad to ask them with you.

We host lectures and discussions around topics of spiritual growth and social justice and are the home base for all Campus Ministries and Religious Groups. Our Exploration of Vocation and Ministry program offers an open and diverse community to reflect upon vocation through bi-weekly peer-group meetings and internships in fields of ministry or nonprofit work or whatever your calling may be.

name: Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. (Xi Omega Chapter)
description:
Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. was founded on the campus of Indiana University on January 5, 1911. Originally chartered and incorporated as Kappa Alpha Nu on April 15, 1911, the name was officially changed to Kappa Alpha Psi on April 15, 1915. The Fraternity's fundamental purpose is ACHIEVEMENT IN EVERY FIELD OF HUMAN ENDEAVOR. Early in this century, African-American students were actively dissuaded from attending college. Formidable obstacles were erected to prevent the enrolled few from assimilating into co-curricular campus life. This ostracism characterized Indiana University in 1911, thus causing Elder W. Diggs, Byron K. Armstrong, and eight other black students to form Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, which remains the only Greek letter organization with its Alpha Chapter on the University's campus. The founders sought a formula that would immediately raise the visions and insight of black collegians at Indiana University and worldwide. Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. has continued to provide leadership in every field of human endeavor.

Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. made a significant impact as the first black Greek organization on the campus of Furman University in Greenville, SC. Brothers Preston Smith and Randy Eaddy (Furman University Board of Directors) were among some of the first brothers on Furman's campus in the late 1970's. Kappa Alpha Psi finally returned to Furman when Corey M. Leathers, Kevin R. Jackson, Bernard Scott II, Chris A. Robertson, and Clayton Gibson III were initiated through the Gamma Nu chapter at Claflin College. The Xi Omega chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. began on February 13, 1994, with the initiation of these five brothers. These brothers returned to Furman University to build and promote the fundamental purpose of achievement and brotherhood for which the Fraternity stands. Since then, the Xi Omega chapter at Furman University has grown and promoted the name of Kappa Alpha Psi through its many scholarly and service-driven achievements. The Xi Omega chapter was chartered on April 26, 1998, by Tyron R. Berrian, Leroy O. Davies-Venn, Mike J. Davis, Alykhan Dhanani, Kenneth S. Generette, Clayton Gibson III, Kevin R. Jackson, Corey M. Leathers, Michael T. McNeil, Daniel Prophete, Christopher A. Robertson, Orlando B. Ruff, Bernard Scott II, Latroy A. Strappy, Randy Williams.

In the Fall of 2021, the Greenville (SC) Alumni chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc. rechartered the Xi Omega chapter. On November 13, 2021, four brothers, Clinton Washington III, Patrick Carolina II, Miles Baker, and Vincent "Duval" McCoy, were initiated into the Fraternity and sought to reignite the continuing legacy of service, brotherhood, and achievement on the campus of Furman University.

For 27 years and counting, the brothers of the Xi Omega chapter of Kappa Alpha Psi Fraternity, Inc., have continued to uphold the legacy of these 15 achievers and those who have come after them by conducting service in the Furman and Greenville, SC, community, developing their characters and becoming notable campus leaders, and excelling in the classroom. Currently, the six exceptional brothers on the yard are determined to maintain the vision their charter brothers and founders of the Fraternity bestowed upon them when they entered Kappaland.

name: Mere Christianity Forum
description:
The mission of Mere Christianity Forum is to promote the thoughtful exploration of Christian faith through conversation & community. Created by Furman students back in 2000, we are a diverse group from a variety of Christian backgrounds and denominations who share a love for rich theological discussion, a commitment to loving and serving our fellow Furman students and the Greenville community, and our interest in finding God in goodness, truth, and beauty. We encourage all kinds of students - seekers, skeptics, and the deeply faithful - to explore the depth and breadth of the Christan faith through our unique blend of faith, reason, and tomfoolery! It's college after all - good old-fashioned fun is an essential part of healthy community!

Check us out at  faithreasontomfoolery.org and vistahouse.org and servantscholars.org and join one of our small groups or come for a CLP Forum!

 

MCF operates in three primary ways:

1) Theological Discussion on campus through CLP events, our weekly "Followship" small groups, our weekly worship nights, and our "Evening With" dinner dialogue events with a Furman professor or community leader at Vista House off campus (www.vistahouse.org).

2) Intentional Christian Community at the Vista House, where we have a residential community during the academic year for Furman juniors and seniors; we also have Game Nights, fellowship dinner events, and brunches.

3) Embodied Christian Practice through serving our fellow students on campus, and through our summer program called Servant Scholars. Go to www.servantscholars.org to learn more!

name: Omicron Delta Kappa
description:
Omicron Delta Kappa was founded in 1914 at Washington and Lee University. The Society recognizes student achievement in five distinct areas: academics and research, athletics, communications, creative and performing arts, and service to campus or community. Membership in ODK includes student leaders from each of these phases of college life. The Furman circle of ODK was added to the national registry in 1981. ODK circles also include faculty and staff members who were inducted into ODK as undergraduates at Furman or other institutions. ODK is a distinctive leadership society and is often referred to as the “Phi Beta Kappa” for student leadership.
Membership
To be eligible for membership in the Furman Circle of ODK, students must:

be in the top 35% of class in academic standing
be a rising sophomore, junior, or senior
Have attained distinction in one or more of the five pillars of campus life (academics and research, athletics, communications, creative and performing arts, and service to campus or community)

Timeline
The nomination process for membership selection for the Furman Circle of ODK occurs during spring term and is completed by the current Furman Circle Membership. New members are notified in June and the induction Ceremony is held the Friday of Family Weekend in the fall semester.
Circle Activities

Circle Meetings (2 per semester)
Signature Service Projects
Signature Leadership Events
ODK National Conference and Scholarship Opportunities
Annual presentation of the Reid and Babb Memorial Awards to outstanding male and female leaders from each class
Opportunities to serve as student officers
Selection of Circle Leader of the Year
summary: Omicron Delta Kappa was founded in 1914 at Washington and Lee University. The Society recognizes student achievement in five distinct areas: academics and research, athletics, communications, creative and performing arts & service to campus or community.

The Student Diversity Council envisions a Furman community that values and embraces all aspects of diversity toward the wellbeing of all community members. To promote such a community, the Student Diversity Council accepts its responsibility in cultivating a campus environment where difference, particularly those based in culture and identity, are uplifted and celebrated.
summary: The Student Diversity Council (SDC) is the umbrella organization for multicultural or identity-based student groups that are committed to diversity, belonging, engagement, and inclusion for all students. Everyone is welcome to join any SDC organization.

name: Student Government Association
description: The mission of Furman Student Government Association (SGA) is to be a proactive governing body that represents Furman's diverse student population and contributes to the positive development of the university community. We are students serving students.
summary: The mission of Furman Student Government Association (SGA) is to be a proactive governing body that represents Furman's diverse student population and contributes to the positive development of the university community. We are students serving students.

name: Student League for Black Culture
description:
Founded in 1973, Student League for Black Culture, known as SLBC, has been dedicated to creating an inviting space for students to truthfully voice their perspectives, connect and learn from one another on a multitude of topics, and ultimately celebrate Black joy in various forms. SLBC exists for the betterment of the wellbeing of Black students at Furman University through camaraderie and engaging measures by educating and uplifting one another. It offers distinctly unique opportunities for creativity and innovativeness through numerous programs hosted throughout the school year while extending reach to the wider Greenville community.  SLBC also strives to connect with all of the organizations within the Student Diversity Council (SDC), with hopes of creating stronger relationships between institutionally marginalized communities at Furman leading to a larger influence of diversity throughout our campus. SLBC strongly adheres to the overall mission of SDC and anyone who wholeheartedly supports that mission is eligible to be a part of the organization. 

 

For the 2025-26 academic year, SLBC will be meeting every other Thursday at 6pm in Trone 208.
summary: SLBC encourages racial interaction, sensitivity, harmony, and education by bringing speakers to campus who have made significant contributions to the enhancement of Black awareness. SLBC encourages the social and cultural interaction of Black students.

name: Student Organization Advisors
description: This portal is intended to be a resource for all student organization advisors.  It will be kept up-to-date with University policies, forms, and other important information regarding student organizations.
summary: This portal is intended to be a resource for all student organization advisors.  It will be kept up-to-date with University policies, forms, and other important information regarding student organizations.

name: The Bell Tower Boys
description: The Bell Tower Boys are an a cappella group composed of students with varying backgrounds, experience, and disciplines. We strive to bring high quality entertainment to the Greenville community while building connections and lifting each other up.
summary: The Bell Tower Boys is Furman's student-led Men's A Cappella ensemble.

name: The Echo, Furman University's Literary Arts Magazine
description:
Since its birth in 1889, The Echo has developed a rich history of serving the Furman community as an esteemed publication of student works.

 

As one of the oldest literary publications in the nation, it serves as a home for conversation and communion among writers, artists and readers.

 

Each year, The Echo seeks to publish innovative works of prose, poetry, studio art, and photography. The magazine is a display of Furman's effort to promote intellectual creativity and academic and artistic excellence amongst the student body.

 

Submissions will open in November, but we invite you to connect with us beforehand! 

 

To read current and past issues of The Echo, visit scholarexchange.furman.edu/echo.

 

To learn about our events and upcoming opportunities, follow our Instagram: @the.furman.echo
summary: The Echo is Furman's annual literary and visual arts magazine (est. 1889). Follow us on Instagram [@the.furman.echo] for updates on events and opportunities!

name: The Paladin
description:
The Paladin is more than just a student news network; it’s the voice of Furman’s students. As Furman University’s only independent student news network, it is our responsibility to offer in-depth coverage of campus news and provide a platform for the content our community needs and wants.

Established in 1916 as a print newspaper, we continue the tradition of providing the student body’s perspective on issues affecting the Furman community in a more-frequent, digital format.

The paper posts articles daily on thepaladin.news .
summary: The Paladin, Furman University's student newspaper, was established in 1916. Today, it continues to provide the student body's perspective on issues affecting the Furman community. The paper posts articles daily on thepaladin.news .

name: The Riley Institute of Government, Leadership and Public Policy
description: The Richard W. Riley Institute of Government, Politics, and Public Leadership is a multi-faceted, non-partisan institute affiliated with the Department of Political Science at Furman University. Named for former Governor of South Carolina and United States Secretary of Education Richard Riley, the Institute is unique in the United States in the emphasis it places on engaging students in the various arenas of politics, public policy, and public leadership.
summary: The Richard W. Riley Institute of Government, Politics, and Public Leadership is a multi-faceted, non-partisan institute affiliated with the Department of Political Science at Furman University. Named for former Governor of South Carolina and United St...

name: The Walking Club
description: With the walk club, we hope to both inspire healthy habits and sustainability within our community. Exercising can be daunting, especially running, and we feel like a club that encourages easier group exercises would be beneficial. We also want to spread awareness about the impact that automobiles have on our campus, and teach about the benefits of walking to class.
summary: A group focused on using walking as a tool for health, sustainability, and friendships.

name: Tocqueville Program
description:
The Tocqueville Program is an intellectual community devoted to seeking clarity about the moral and philosophic questions at the heart of political life.  We host curricular and extracurricular activities designed to help students and faculty to engage seriously with the most powerful arguments behind diverse and competing religious, political and ethical points of view.  Our work is undertaken in the hope that the practice of shared, disciplined inquiry into disputed questions can help us understand better how to maintain the delicate fabric of our civilization.

Our program takes its name from Alexis de Tocqueville, a 19th-century French author, statesman, and traveler who developed a “new science of politics” focused on the study of the modern democratic soul.  On the contested, partisan questions of his time, Tocqueville “undertook to see, not differently, but further than the parties.”  We seek to follow his example.

name: Trone Student Center
description: The Trone Student Center is the hub of campus activity at Furman. Grab a cup of coffee at Starbucks, hang out at Barnes & Noble, get lunch at the PalaDen, enjoy a late night snack in The Paddock, attend a CLP in Watkins Room, pick up your mail at the P2X, catch a movie at Burgiss Theater, or simply hang out here at the TSC. This is YOUR center for student life, so we'll see you at the Trone!
summary: The Trone Student Center is the living room of campus. The Trone has numerous spaces to accommodate any need: studying, eating, relaxing, events, etc. Make sure to visit us and enjoy any of our amazing offerings and the unforgettable views of Swan Lake.

name: UKirk Furman
description:
Associated with the PC(USA), UKirk Furman is a family of faith encouraged by and committed to: -Wrestling with Scripture, acknowledging its authority, and trusting the Holy Spirit to speak through it -Experiencing God's grace and witnessing Christ's love as we seek to serve other whether at Furman, in Greenville, or throughout the world -Worshipping and studying the living, Triune God through food, fun, and fellowship.

name: Unity
description: Unity is meant to serve as a safe home, a way to connect students of color at Furman University. Unity mentors will provide a safe space to share experiences and share insight on how to navigate spaces in which they are the minority. Mentors are to foster relationships with students, demonstrate active listening, and guide students on their four-year pathway. Moreover, Unity encourages mentors to demonstrate upstanding character and seize learning opportunities from their mentee(s). This organization stands to teach others to do the same: stand up for their differences and wear them proudly.
summary: Unity is meant to serve as a safe home, a way to connect students of color at Furman University. Unity mentors will provide a safe space to share experiences and share insight on how to navigate spaces in which they are the minority.

name: Women's Club Basketball
description: To give women the opportunity to participate in basketball tournaments, games, and practices to better themselves in the sport of basketball, while playing at a more competitive level than intramurals. Practice with be held once-twice a week while giving women the opportunity to participate in both home and away tournaments.

name: Women's Club Volleyball
description: The Furman Women's Club Volleyball team practices 1-2 times a week for an hour and a half (typically Tuesdays and/or Thursdays) We participate in 2-4 tournaments per semester. Tryouts for the 2025-26 academic year will be in the Fall. Follow our social media to stay up-to-date! Insta: @furmanclubvolleyball

name: Women’s chorale
description: This group meets twice a week from 4:00-6:00p.m. The director is Dr. Vivian Hamilton and the manager is Rachel Hughes. In order to join this ensemble you will need to be able to commit to the bi-weekly rehearsals as well as the two concerts we perform during the year. By being a part of this group, you will be able to learn and perform amazing music while making lasting friendships and memories.
summary: This is a women only choral ensemble sponsored by the music department. Any woman with basic musicianship skills and prior musical experience who is interested in being part of a wonderful group and making beautiful music is encouraged to join!

name: Writing & Media Lab
description:
The Writing & Media Lab is an academic department staffed by Furman students who are trained to help their peers with writing and multimedia assignments, from papers to videos to podcasts and more.

 

Starting February 11 at 6:00pm, the WML will begin offering a new Writing Development Forum! This will be a voluntary group that meets weekly to discuss time management tips and writing strategies, with a focus on the development of long-term writing projects (theses, term projects, creative work, etc). If this group interests you, request to join our organization here on SyncDIN!
summary: The Writing & Media Lab is an academic department staffed by Furman students who are trained to help their peers with writing and multimedia assignments, from papers to videos to podcasts and more.

name: Young Life
description: Young Life is an relational ministry that introduces high school students to Jesus Christ. We help Christ followers to grow and mature in their faith through fellowship, bible study, and prayer.
summary: Young Life is an relational ministry that introduces high school students to Jesus Christ. We help Christ followers to grow and mature in their faith through fellowship, bible study, and prayer.

name: Zeta Tau Alpha
description: Sisterhood, love, and friendship. These are the words that come to mind when our members think of Zeta Tau Alpha. Although the ZTA experience begins in college, it extends far beyond four years. The ZTA experience is made up of many parts. Sisters are connected to a large network of over 235,000 women, which provides countless opportunities. The bonds of friendship that are formed in both collegiate and alumnae chapters last a lifetime. Women develop leadership skills by taking on responsibility both within ZTA and in their communities. The Fraternity and ZTA Foundation support members’ growth through educational programming and opportunities to serve others and promote breast cancer education and awareness. Members of ZTA are encouraged to follow their passion, and their sisters are there to support those goals. We joined the Greek community in Spring of 2015, and since then have continued to foster an environment of love, friendship, and service. Explore our website to find out more about ZTA, our chapter, upcoming events and our philanthropy. The ZTA experience is truly a unique one. Take a look and experience the possibilities.
summary: Sisterhood, love, and friendship.
